notable_absence.finding: The 'Testing' section is a single, contentless sentence under its own H2 heading ('Integrate developing with the Java SDK into your accustomed test framework.') with no code, no links, and no concrete guidance at all - a named section that is effectively a placeholder, unlike every other section on the page.

cross_component_finding: This page resolves the open question flagged in concept-docs/response-time-observability.json's own extraction: its 'Threshold Logging' section and that page's 'Request Tracing' section are confirmed to be the SAME underlying default tracer mechanism (sdk:request-tracer), not two different concepts - this page's own text ties its example log line's `total_us` field directly to 'tracing values such as `total_us`', explicitly using the word 'tracing' to describe what its Threshold Log line reports. Reused sdk:request-tracer here rather than minting a second sdk:threshold-logging concept for what is textually confirmed to be one mechanism described on two different concept-docs pages with two differently-shaped example log lines.
cross_product_finding: The page presents RBAC/roles/authentication as one unified model spanning both self-managed Server (RBAC, credentials, roles, privileges) and Capella (organizations, projects, access privileges) under a single 'Security' heading, with only a subsection-header change ('Capella Security & Privileges') marking the deployment-model switch - unlike the sharp Capella-vs-self-managed prerequisite divergence (differing minimum-version and NTP requirements) that round 4 found on the transactions howto page, this page does not call out any concrete difference between the two RBAC surfaces beyond naming them separately.
